content.title: Olivier Rioux: Top facts you did not know about 7'9" Canadian NBA prospect
content.text: The 19-year-old Florida Gators freshman has officially become the tallest player ever in US college basketball, standing at 7 feet, 9 inches (2.4m). Find out more about the Canadian teen and his NCAA debut.By Chloe MerrellUpdated on 09 November 2025 05:00 GMT-65 min readOlivier Rioux is used to being the centre of attention. At 7 feet and 9 inches (240 cm) tall, the 19-year-old from Canada regularly walks out of the door only to be stopped and asked to appear in photos such is his height. After all, he is the world's tallest teenager. And now, as a college basketball freshman at the University of Florida, Rioux is already breaking records and being tipped as a new giant of the basketball world. He made his debut in the NCAA on Thursday, 6 November, in a 104-64 victory for the Florida Gators over North Florida - becoming officially the tallest player ever to play in US college basketball. Though he never actually touched the ball. The redshirt freshman entered the game with just two minutes remaining, following repeated chants from the home fans of "we want Ollie", demanding he appear on court. “It felt great,” Rioux said. “The support from everybody was amazing, even on the bench and even the fans. I think everybody supported me. I’m very grateful," the AP reported. When asked about the significance of his history making appearance, he responded: “It’s another day, I guess.” Kenny George, at 7 feet, 7 inches held the previous record of tallest player in college basketball. As the young star readies to begin a college hoops career sure to capture the imagination of basketball fans worldwide, here’s what you might not know about the future fan favourite. NBA season preview 2024-25: Top teams and stars to watch, schedules and more Six international stars to watch during the 2024-25 NBA season Olivier Rioux: Tall origins Born on 2 February 2006, in Quebec, Canada, there were early signs that Rioux would grow up to be something special. Weighing 7.5 pounds (3.4kg) at birth, according to Guinness World Records, Rioux grew to 16 pounds (7.3kg) in his first month alone. And he didn’t stop there. By the fifth grade, the young Canadian was already 5ft 2in and at 15 years old, he stood at 7ft 5in officially becoming the world’s tallest teenager. Was it always to be that Rioux would hold such a prize? “We’re still not 100 per cent sure why I’m so tall,” he told Guinness in 2022. “After investigation, doctors could only explain it with the genetics that my family has.” Rioux’s father stands at 6ft 8in, his mum at 6ft 2in, while his older brother is 6ft 9in. “We’re a pretty tall family,” he added. The basketball player has also said that having tall family members helps him navigate the attention that comes his way. “You don’t have a single three seconds to yourself when you’re outside, which I was fine with because my brother and my dad are tall. And, as a family, we used to go out. That’s just how it was, and you can’t change that because people are curious,” Rioux told the AP.Picture by 2023 Getty ImagesFrance's Victor Wembayanama is among one of the tallest active players in the NBA this seasonOlivier Rioux: Taller than other NBA legends The sport of basketball, where Rioux hopes to make his mark, is well known for being the stomping ground of giants but how exactly does he compare to his peers? If Rioux were to step out and play on an NBA court tomorrow, he would be the tallest player competing - and by some margin. He is five inches taller than the current tallest man in the league, Zach Edey, and holds six inches over reigning NBA rookie of the year Victor Wembanyama. Rioux even supplants famed leviathans Gheorghe Muresan (7ft 7in) and Yao Ming (7ft 6in). Size 20 shoes and custom-made items Big super-sized has meant the Rioux has had to adjust the world around him so he might fit in. That includes his bed at home which has been tailored to fit his size. Other notable changes he has to make include ducking under most doorways he walks through and trying to find size 20 shoes to fit his feet.Olivier Rioux: Already representing Canada Having grown so much so early on, it’s with little surprise that Rioux has already taken to the court for Canada. His basketball journey first began at the age of five and saw him move to the IMG Academy in Sarasota, Florida before joining the Florida Gators. In between, he has competed in a string of FIBA events including helping Canada to bronze medals at the Under-16 Americas Championship and the 2023 Under-18 FIBA AmeriCup Championship. NBA acclaim While the NBA, the promised land for all basketball players, may glitter on the horizon for Rioux, any future connection with the premier US basketball league won’t be the first the teenager has made. Former NBA champion and fellow Canadian Jamal Murray once asked Rioux for a photo when he first the young star at 12 years old. Rioux was then 6ft 10in. Sharing the picture of the two of them in 2023 just as Murray won the NBA title with the Denver Nuggets, Rioux wrote: “Congrats to Jamal Murray for winning the Nba Championship with Denver ! Do you remember 5 years ago you were the one asking for the picture 😂”
